 Liberty Capital (GLIB.A) Could Be 51% Undervalued As Profit Returns And Buyback Begins
 Bailey Pemberton Sun, November 8, 2026 at 12:11 AM CST 4 min read GLIBA +6.76% 
 Trade GLIBA on Coinbase Trading disclosure Trading disclosure

 Learn more Liberty Capital (GLIB.A) reported a return to profitability and announced a new capital return plan, posting Q3 net income of US$27 million and authorizing up to US$100 million in share repurchases. 
 Liberty Capital's latest earnings and capital return moves have come alongside a sharp rebound in the share price, with a 1 day share price return of 6.6% and a 30 day share price return of 31.1% lifting the stock to US$26.33. However, the total shareholder return over the past year is still down 20.9%, suggesting recent optimism is building off a weak starting point rather than a long winning streak. 
 See how Liberty Capital's rebound compares to other potential turnaround plays by reviewing our hand picked list of 38 high quality undervalued stocks . 
 Bulls argue Liberty Capital's profit return and fresh buyback signal a genuine reset. Bears see a short squeeze on thin fundamentals. The recent surge sets the stage for the key debate: what does the valuation actually say? 
 Most Popular Narrative: 51% Undervalued 
 At a last close of $26.33 against a narrative fair value of $54, Liberty Capital is framed as heavily discounted, which puts the recent share price rebound in a very different light. 
 Rural broadband build outs such as AIRRAQ 1 and Alaska plan commitments, together with provisional awards of approximately US$120 million in BEAD funding that would offset capital costs, position the company to serve previously unserved locations with less pressure on its own balance sheet. This can help protect free cash flow and long term earnings. 
 See why 1 investors see Liberty Capital as 51% undervalued . 
 The most followed narrative applies an 8.09% discount rate to those projected cash flows and arrives at a fair value of $54. That implies a 51.2% discount to this estimate, with the thesis hinging on modest 2.5% annual revenue growth, a move in profit margin toward 16.9%, and a future P/E of 17.4x by 2029. 
 Analysts behind this narrative also assume earnings reach $188.3 million and that Liberty Capital trades on a multiple slightly above the current US Telecom sector level. That combination of mid single digit top line growth and higher profitability is what needs to line up for the valuation gap to close according to this framework. 
 Result: Fair Value of $54 (UNDERVALUED) 
 Still, the Liberty Capital story can break if wireless substitution and Starlink style competition keep chipping away at fixed data customers, or if heavy Alaska plan spending remains above management's 15% to 20% CapEx target and constrains cash generation for longer than current narratives allow.
